newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police detain minority party members in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Police detain minority party members in Indonesia.

text.p: Police clashed with knife-wielding supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) in east Java after detaining a PPP member in the Indonesian general election campaign, police said on Tuesday.

The disturbance came as the government and the three political parties legally permitted to contest the May 29 elections agreed on Monday there had been a number of rule infringements since the campaign opened on April 27.

The clash at Panjentek, about 60 km (37 miles) southeast of Indonesia's second city of Surabaya, was the latest in a series of election disturbances, mainly involving the PPP and the ruling Golkar, which is expected to win easily.
The third party, the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), is riven by internal strife and appears to have had little impact in the campaign.

The parties are vying for the votes of the 125 million electorate to fill 425 elected seats in the 500-seat House of Representatives. The other 75 seats are alloted to the military which does not vote.
Political analysts said the incidents so far had mainly involved turf battles between high-spirited political rivals or had stemmed from banned motorcades causing traffic chaos.
Police in Panjentek said about 500 PPP supporters surrounded the police station on Monday, apparently after hearing a PPP member was being held following a crackdown on motorcades.

"The situation is now safe again, but yesterday they came with knives and sickles. They were dispersed by police and a number of those with weapons were detained," a policeman, who did not identify himself, told Reuters.
Republika newspaper reported on Tuesday that police had detained 53 people and "tens" of people had suffered heavy injuries in the clash.
But the policeman said only a number of light injuries were reported. He declined to say how many were still in detention.
A number of vehicles were damaged by the crowd, he added, but there was no widespread vandalism.
Attorney-General Singgih (Eds: one word), head of the election supervision committee, told party leaders on Monday there had been a number of violations of election regulations.
The official Antara news agency quoted him as saying those responsible might have been outsiders and not party members.
Interior Minister Yogie Memet, also head of the General Election Institute running the poll, attended the meeting with PPP, Golkar and PDI leaders.
"Improve your campaigning and stop the violations," Memet told the parties.
Armed Forces chief General Fiesal Tanjung gave contestants a fresh warning, saying there had to be no more street parades or motorcades.
"All procedures have been clearly spelled out. Street rallies and motorcades are prohibited," Tanjung was quoted as saying.
